endorsements.quote: Translational trials that include a silent testing phase, wherein a model’s performance is evaluated prospectively in its clinical context without impacting patient care or workflow as the model output is not shown to end-users, may be warranted as part of the evaluation process before full implementation 41 , 42 .

Protocols should define when ambient listening is appropriate, ensure patients are informed and provide consent to recording, and establish alternative processes for those who decline, ensuring their care remains timely and unaffected 48 .
Hence, institutions must define accountability structures and ensure clinicians carefully review the generated text.

In the absence of explicit guidance, health systems need to define what to retain, the duration of retention, and access controls, with clear distinction between transient processing data and records incorporated into the medical records that are legally binding.
Early user engagement to tailor interfaces, workflows, and outputs to the realities of clinical practice are necessary.
Ambient scribes need to adapt to local vernacular by contextual training and customization.
Health systems should consider including qualitative metrics that captures conciseness usability of documents, beyond simply time savings.
Testing of proprietary models across different practice settings should be conducted with the goal of ensuring fairness across different patient demographics.
Audit trails and real-time monitoring will be essential.
Security and governance frameworks will need to specify role-based access and restrictions, data encryption, and establish breach response protocols.

unlisted_practices: Develop high-quality domain-specific benchmarks for ambient scribes that incorporate accuracy, clinical relevance, and potential for harm.
Develop international consensus standards for ambient scribe technical performance, documentation quality, patient safety, and ethical compliance.
Establish clear contractual agreements between vendors and health systems to mitigate risks of cross-border data flows.
Vendors should design ambient scribe systems that encourage review and validation of documentation and make the provenance of information transparent.
Avoid creating dual documentation that leaves audio recordings and transcripts as shadow records.
Use LLM-based evaluators, overseen by interdisciplinary governance bodies, to augment expert review of ambient scribe notes and flag notes for manual inspection.
Monitor ambient scribe performance drift, equity, and unsafe acceptance of scribe-generated content.
Require trainees to independently generate clinical documents in an AI-free phase before using AI scribes.
Organizations should collaborate internationally to share knowledge and standardize implementation of ambient scribes across settings.
Explicitly disclose and obtain agreement for ambient scribe use in jurisdictions requiring two-party consent.
